issues: Persistent React hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' — JSX instrumentation injects a <span style=display:contents> around interpolated text in <option>{a.name} ({a.tag_id})</option>. Cosmetic console warning, does not affect functionality.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is ~1290 lines; overdue for split into routers (auth, org, requisitions, files, assets, grns, handovers, notifications, pdf).

download_file / requisition_pdf / handover_pdf / assets_summary_pdf still accept ?auth=<jwt> query fallback — JWTs in URLs can leak into access logs and Referer headers. Replace with short-lived signed download tokens or drop the query fallback since axios uses httpOnly cookies via withCredentials anyway.

create_handover has no validation that a linked asset_id is currently in_stock — a super_admin could re-handover an already-assigned or pending_receipt asset, silently overwriting pending_handover_id and orphaning the earlier notification. Add: assert asset.status == 'in_stock' and not asset.pending_receipt before flipping to pending.

confirm_notification does not check that the notification is still 'unread'/'pending' — re-clicking Yes after receipt keeps toggling pending_receipt=False and re-writing assigned fields (idempotent for now but hides bugs). Consider guarding on n['status'] not in ('confirmed',).

list_notifications is scoped by user_id, but that field is only populated when the handover employee_name matches a seeded user (case-insensitive exact match). Users whose display name deviates (e.g. 'M.A Quieum' vs 'MA Quieum') will silently miss notifications. Consider matching on email or a user_id field entered at handover time.

NotificationBell polling shows every unread asset_receipt notification via seen ref; if a user has 5 pending, only the first pops. UX would benefit from stacking (chained modal) or explicit 'X of Y' indicator.
SignaturePad only supports mouse/touch on <canvas> but does not resize for HiDPI screens (canvas is 320x120 fixed pixels), signatures can look aliased in PDF.
